facts.fact: Broadcast stations must offer candidates their lowest unit rate during the 45 days before a primary election.
facts.quote: During the 45 days before a primary and 60 days before a general election, broadcast stations must offer candidates their lowest unit rate for the same class and amount of time.

facts.fact: The lowest unit rate requirement applies only to broadcast stations and does not apply to CTV, streaming platforms, or digital advertising.
facts.quote: One important distinction: the lowest unit rate applies only to broadcast stations. It does not apply to CTV, streaming platforms, or digital advertising.

facts.fact: Under the FEC 'stand by your ad' rule, a candidate voiceover TV ad must show a clearly identifiable image of the candidate for at least four seconds.
facts.quote: a candidate voiceover with a "clearly identifiable photographic or similar image" of the candidate visible for at least four seconds.

facts.fact: The federal 'stand by your ad' requirement applies only to candidates for president, Senate, and House.
facts.quote: the federal "stand by your ad" rule applies only to candidates for president, Senate, and House.

facts.fact: Broadcast sponsorship identification for paid political content is required under 47 CFR 73.1212.
facts.quote: Under 47 CFR 73.1212, every broadcast of paid political content must include a sponsorship identification announcement.

facts.fact: Bona fide news coverage, including newscasts and news interviews, does not trigger equal time obligations under FCC Section 315(a)(1)-(4).
facts.quote: Bona fide news coverage, including newscasts, news interviews, documentaries, and on-the-spot news events, doesn't trigger equal time obligations (FCC Section 315(a)(1)-(4)).

facts.fact: Federal candidates have a right to reasonable access to purchase airtime on broadcast stations under Section 312(a)(7), a provision that applies only to federal candidates.
facts.quote: Under FCC Section 312(a)(7), broadcast licensees must provide "reasonable access" to legally qualified candidates for federal office.

facts.fact: Broadcast stations must keep a public political file recording ad requests, including the sponsor, airtime schedule, rate charged, and classes of time purchased.
facts.quote: These records include the name of the candidate or issue, the sponsor of the ad, the schedule of airtime purchased, the rate charged, and the classes of time purchased.

facts.fact: Under Section 315(a), broadcast stations cannot censor ads that are candidate 'uses,' while third-party PAC and issue ads may be rejected at the station's discretion.
facts.quote: This protection applies specifically to candidate "uses," not to ads from PACs, Super PACs, or issue advocacy groups. Those third-party ads can be rejected by stations at their discretion.

facts.fact: The FCC's political advertising rules are based on the Communications Act of 1934.
facts.quote: The FCC's political advertising rules are based on the Communications Act of 1934.

facts.fact: The page recommends that campaigns keep their own parallel records of political ad buys for at least two years.

facts.fact: Broadcast TV stations must keep political files for the duration of the license period, which is typically eight years for TV stations.

facts.fact: Washington state's Public Disclosure Commission requires sponsor identification on all political ads appearing on commercial advertisers, including digital platforms.
